nodes.rationale: Later slices thicken the real path rather than creating independent unused libraries; pooling claims wait for proven identity and state isolation.

nodes.label: pg_query 18.1.0 behind an adapter
nodes.rationale: Favors PostgreSQL 18 grammar coverage over a pure Rust build (sqlparser runner up); the native code must be isolated, bounded, reviewed and fuzzed.

nodes.label: Shared process failure domain
nodes.rationale: Accepted consequence of one daemon; bounded probe tasks, timeouts and resource limits reduce the risk and process isolation remains a future extraction option.

nodes.label: Failover safety KPI (zero unfenced promotions or silent replays)
nodes.norm_label: failover safety kpi (zero unfenced promotions or silent replays)

nodes.norm_label: pgbench and purpose built workload generator

nodes.norm_label: core mvp (correct primary proxy with session reuse)

nodes.label: Pgpool-II 4.7.3 functional baseline
nodes.rationale: Selected as the functional baseline without claiming 100 percent parity or a full source/runtime audit.

nodes.label: Private vulnerability reporting channel (not yet configured)
nodes.norm_label: private vulnerability reporting channel (not yet configured)

nodes.label: Security triage scope
nodes.rationale: A correctness issue that can corrupt or expose data is security relevant even if memory safety is intact.

nodes.label: Session pooling (one frontend owns one backend lease)
nodes.norm_label: session pooling (one frontend owns one backend lease)
nodes.rationale: First safe mode because it preserves a real backend session throughout a client connection; it gives less backend reduction than transaction multiplexing and that limit is accepted explicitly.

nodes.label: Safe first party Rust (forbid unsafe, rustfmt, Clippy)
nodes.norm_label: safe first party rust (forbid unsafe, rustfmt, clippy)
nodes.rationale: Native parser, TLS provider and SQLite dependencies need their own boundary review; a safe wrapper is not proof that its internals are safe.

nodes.label: Merged or deferred candidate crates (no common crate)
nodes.norm_label: merged or deferred candidate crates (no common crate)
nodes.rationale: Candidates start as modules inside core or control; extraction needs independent consumers, dependency weight, versioning, ownership or isolation needs and a documented decision.
nodes.source_location: Merge or defer the candidate crates

nodes.label: Modular daemon with independent CLI decision
nodes.norm_label: modular daemon with independent cli decision
nodes.rationale: Chosen for the four VM scenario, small operational surface and vertical delivery; the separate controller executable is deferred until multiple proxies need a single authority.

nodes.label: Architecture options considered
nodes.rationale: Separate proxy and controller services need cross process auth and reconciliation before the first proxy works; orchestrating existing poolers misses the Rust protocol goal; reproducing Pgpool imports legacy constraints and a large parity burden.

nodes.label: Overhead investigation triggers (10 percent TPS, 1 ms p99)
nodes.norm_label: overhead investigation triggers (10 percent tps, 1 ms p99)
nodes.rationale: Numeric triggers are lab investigation goals, not published performance claims; correctness gates are mandatory even if performance exceeds expectations.

nodes.label: Release gates
nodes.rationale: Failed gates keep a feature planned or in progress; documentation alone never changes it to Implemented/Tested.

nodes.label: Configured backend registration
nodes.rationale: DNS changes alone do not establish cluster membership; system identity is validated before admitting a new backend.

nodes.label: Backend health state machine (Unknown, Healthy, Suspect, Unavailable, Recovering)
nodes.norm_label: backend health state machine (unknown, healthy, suspect, unavailable, recovering)

nodes.label: Replication freshness and byte lag
nodes.rationale: Time since replay is misleading on a stopped workload, so source freshness and byte lag are used; the 16 MiB eligibility threshold is not a causal consistency guarantee.

nodes.label: Weighted round robin replica selection
nodes.rationale: First policy; least active leases is the next experiment and least latency is later because feedback can oscillate.

nodes.label: Eventual read consistency for replica sessions
nodes.norm_label: eventual read consistency for replica sessions
nodes.rationale: Lag thresholds screen new session admission only; an LSN based causal token is deferred rather than approximated by a time based sticky window.

nodes.label: Operator managed principal to backend login map
nodes.norm_label: operator managed principal to backend login map
nodes.rationale: Unmapped combinations fail; startup strings alone cannot select credentials.

nodes.label: No primary fallback for replica profiles
nodes.norm_label: no primary fallback for replica profiles
nodes.rationale: A future primary fallback would need independently enforced read restrictions that survive role changes and a new explicit decision.

nodes.label: Critical path (protocol state, auth identity, cleanup, routing semantics, promotion safety)
nodes.norm_label: critical path (protocol state, auth identity, cleanup, routing semantics, promotion safety)
nodes.rationale: Do not parallelize conflicting implementations of the same lease or topology authority.

nodes.label: One daemon with separate modules plus separate CLI
nodes.norm_label: one daemon with separate modules plus separate cli
nodes.rationale: Single daemon process boundary confirmed; split processes deferred.

nodes.label: Dependency boundaries (acyclic crate graph)
nodes.rationale: Protocol does not depend on control or administration; core does not read SQLite; control does not consume frontend query bytes; admin mutations share the operation service with the CLI; exporters cannot block leases.

nodes.label: Release practices
nodes.rationale: Pre 1.0 releases while contracts evolve; a version number is not a safety certification; promote only tagged artifacts with checksums, SBOM, license notices and reproducible evidence.

nodes.label: Initial four VM lab
nodes.rationale: Four VMs on one Proxmox host share a host failure domain; replication alone cannot survive that host's loss.

nodes.label: All-writer write barrier
nodes.rationale: A final flush target can only be claimed after a barrier covering every writer path, including connections that bypass POOL; draining POOL alone is insufficient.

nodes.label: Candidate and RPO policy
nodes.rationale: Highest LSN alone cannot establish that every acknowledged commit survived; no zero data loss claim is inferred from asynchronous replication.

nodes.label: Fencing contract (allowlisted adapter)
nodes.rationale: A successful power off request is insufficient without verified completion and exclusion from automatic restart or another writer path.

nodes.label: Promotion operation stages (Plan, Quiesce, Fence, Revalidate, Promote, Reconcile, Recover)
nodes.norm_label: promotion operation stages (plan, quiesce, fence, revalidate, promote, reconcile, recover)

nodes.label: Operational V1 (four VM scenario with replica routing and fenced manual promotion)
nodes.norm_label: operational v1 (four vm scenario with replica routing and fenced manual promotion)

nodes.label: Manual failover policy
nodes.rationale: A transport timeout or failed health probe never authorizes promotion; PostgreSQL requires preventing the former primary from returning as another primary.

nodes.label: pg_query 18.1.0 and libpg_query (PostgreSQL raw parser)
nodes.rationale: Recommended because it uses the actual PostgreSQL raw parser; costs are C/FFI native build, catalog blind semantics and mixed native licenses.

nodes.label: Dependency adoption gate
nodes.rationale: Before installing, re-verify version, features, MSRV, advisories, native deps and licenses; commit Cargo.lock, generate an SBOM; first party Rust forbids unsafe with documented native exceptions.

nodes.label: Hybrid parser policy
nodes.rationale: Parse with pg_query, use session state and declared read profile, and enforce database constraints; server enforcement cannot contain extension side effects so an operator trust contract remains.

nodes.label: SQLite WAL operation journal (synchronous FULL)
nodes.rationale: Acknowledged journal operations must survive process and power loss; WAL is local concurrency, not distributed coordination.

nodes.label: Baseline gaps (planning inventory, not parity certification)
nodes.norm_label: baseline gaps (planning inventory, not parity certification)

nodes.label: PCP commands, SQL commands and pgpool_adm reference surface
nodes.norm_label: pcp commands, sql commands and pgpool_adm reference surface

nodes.label: Other configuration surfaces (HBA, PCP credentials, PAM, LDAP)
nodes.norm_label: other configuration surfaces (hba, pcp credentials, pam, ldap)
nodes.rationale: POOL defines a new authenticated administration contract; PAM and LDAP are deferred, default deny rules, SCRAM/TLS and explicit identity mapping come first.

nodes.label: License and source reuse policy
nodes.rationale: Implement from documented behavior first; before copying source inspect the exact file, retain notices, record origin and review compatibility. A permissive top level license does not describe every vendored file.

nodes.label: Structured allowlisted adapter disposition for command options
nodes.norm_label: structured allowlisted adapter disposition for command options
nodes.rationale: Shell command options (failover_command, follow_primary_command, if_up_cmd, ssl_passphrase_command and similar) become structured allowlisted adapters or an external supervisor; no API supplied arbitrary shell.

nodes.label: Automatic promotion (not ready for initial release)
nodes.norm_label: automatic promotion (not ready for initial release)
nodes.rationale: Requires an independent safety case, distributed authority, fencing and partition testing.

nodes.label: Manual promotion (feasible with external dependencies)
nodes.rationale: Needs verified fencing, durable operations, timeline checks, RPO disclosure and restart reconciliation.

nodes.label: Query result caching (high uncertainty)
nodes.rationale: External writers, permissions, MVCC snapshots and invalidation cannot be solved by TTL alone.

nodes.label: Session pooling feasibility (high feasibility, high correctness risk)
nodes.norm_label: session pooling feasibility (high feasibility, high correctness risk)

nodes.label: Transparent arbitrary read splitting (low confidence)
nodes.rationale: Catalog dependent semantics, session state, prepared statements and causal consistency require a narrower contract.

nodes.label: Failover and recovery option family (15 options)
nodes.norm_label: failover and recovery option family (15 options)
nodes.rationale: Manual fenced operations first; recovery and automatic failback deferred.

nodes.label: Query cache option family (13 options)
nodes.rationale: Disabled and deferred pending an invalidation and consistency contract.

nodes.label: Connections and identity option family (48 options)
nodes.norm_label: connections and identity option family (48 options)
nodes.rationale: Mapped to typed endpoint, limit, identity and TLS policy equivalents with no Pgpool syntax compatibility; process model options map to async admission and backend budgets.

nodes.label: Logs, files and reset option family (28 options)
nodes.norm_label: logs, files and reset option family (28 options)
nodes.rationale: Structured redacted logs and reset lifecycle; statement and message logging are unsafe behaviors not enabled by default.

nodes.label: Relation metadata option family (6 options)
nodes.rationale: Bounded metadata and conservative uncertainty; not a query result cache.

nodes.label: Canonical runtime declaration census (RT-001 to RT-186)
nodes.norm_label: canonical runtime declaration census (rt-001 to rt-186)

nodes.label: Source-only delta names (hidden aliases, health_check_test, replication_mode)
nodes.norm_label: source-only delta names (hidden aliases, health_check_test, replication_mode)

nodes.label: Streaming and health option family (24 options)
nodes.norm_label: streaming and health option family (24 options)
nodes.rationale: Authenticated probes, freshness and lag thresholds; follow-primary actions remain explicit operations.

nodes.label: Streaming sample census (CFG-001 to CFG-207, 207 spellings)
nodes.norm_label: streaming sample census (cfg-001 to cfg-207, 207 spellings)

nodes.label: Watchdog option family (55 options)
nodes.rationale: Future external coordination and endpoint HA; no copied Watchdog config or half-quorum policy.

nodes.label: External etcd for later HA (no consensus in initial proxy)
nodes.norm_label: external etcd for later ha (no consensus in initial proxy)
nodes.rationale: OpenRaft enlarges POOL's responsibility; a lease alone cannot stop a paused old leader from promoting, so fencing and operation epochs remain required.

nodes.label: SQL classification through PostgreSQL 18 raw grammar
nodes.norm_label: sql classification through postgresql 18 raw grammar
nodes.rationale: Classification is not an authorization engine; views, rules, RLS, functions and FDW side effects cannot be proven safe by a raw AST.

nodes.label: Bounded channels, buffers, tasks and queues
nodes.norm_label: bounded channels, buffers, tasks and queues

nodes.label: Axum REST administration API plus CLI
nodes.norm_label: axum rest administration api plus cli
nodes.rationale: Protected local transport and mTLS for remote exposure; PCP compatibility deferred.

nodes.label: First deployment: one proxy VM, primary and two replicas on Proxmox
nodes.norm_label: first deployment: one proxy vm, primary and two replicas on proxmox

nodes.label: V1 milestone (four VM scenario with manual fenced failover)
nodes.norm_label: v1 milestone (four vm scenario with manual fenced failover)
nodes.rationale: V1 can stay on manual failover indefinitely; automatic promotion is an optional product decision.

nodes.label: Drain, detach and attach node operations
nodes.norm_label: drain, detach and attach node operations

nodes.label: Two observed primaries close write admission
nodes.norm_label: two observed primaries close write admission

nodes.label: Separation of observed health/role from maintenance and desired membership
nodes.norm_label: separation of observed health/role from maintenance and desired membership

nodes.label: FenceReceipt
nodes.rationale: Unfenced promotion can create two writable primaries; the receipt must be independently validated for the exact old-primary infrastructure identity.

nodes.label: Failover operation phases (Planned to Completed or Failed/NeedsReview)
nodes.norm_label: failover operation phases (planned to completed or failed/needsreview)

nodes.label: PromotionPlan
nodes.rationale: Operator approval is bound to plan hash, target, expected epoch, RPO disclosure and expiration.

nodes.label: Candidate replica leases retired before promotion
nodes.norm_label: candidate replica leases retired before promotion

nodes.label: Equivalents for the 15 PCP operations
nodes.rationale: CLI and REST equivalents replace the PCP wire protocol, which is not implemented in V1.

nodes.label: Versioned REST administration API (/v1) and CLI
nodes.norm_label: versioned rest administration api (/v1) and cli

nodes.label: Viewer, operator, promoter and configuration role authorization
nodes.norm_label: viewer, operator, promoter and configuration role authorization

nodes.label: Fuzzing and native boundary sanitizer tests
nodes.norm_label: fuzzing and native boundary sanitizer tests

nodes.label: Operations journal crash and disk fault tests
nodes.norm_label: operations journal crash and disk fault tests

nodes.label: Routing differential and adversarial corpus tests
nodes.norm_label: routing differential and adversarial corpus tests

nodes.label: Persisted approved writer, epoch and quarantine
nodes.norm_label: persisted approved writer, epoch and quarantine
nodes.rationale: Observed role was confused with authorized writer after restart; durable authorization must agree with fresh probes and incomplete effects are reconciled.

nodes.label: SQLite journal for operations, audit and approved writer/epoch/quarantine
nodes.norm_label: sqlite journal for operations, audit and approved writer/epoch/quarantine
nodes.rationale: Local persistence stores durable authorization but never observed backend role truth; bootstrap once and reconcile with fresh roles before restart admission.

nodes.label: No silent replay of uncertain work (lost COMMIT response)
nodes.norm_label: no silent replay of uncertain work (lost commit response)
nodes.rationale: If the backend response is lost after COMMIT, the client observes connection loss; POOL never retries or reports a definite rollback.

nodes.label: Bounded authenticated probes with dedicated monitor role
nodes.norm_label: bounded authenticated probes with dedicated monitor role
nodes.rationale: Reachability alone cannot identify a safe writable primary or a sufficiently current replica; probes observe role, system identity, timeline and WAL positions.

nodes.label: Health failure alone produces no promotion
nodes.norm_label: health failure alone produces no promotion
nodes.rationale: Monitoring failures are kept separate from administrative mutation authority.

nodes.label: Lag computed only for comparable fresh positions; missing evidence is unknown
nodes.norm_label: lag computed only for comparable fresh positions; missing evidence is unknown
nodes.rationale: No freshness guarantee is derived only from time since last replay; expired or missing WAL evidence excludes replica admission.

nodes.label: Approved writer, epoch and quarantine authority
nodes.norm_label: approved writer, epoch and quarantine authority
nodes.rationale: Immutable snapshots publish only when fresh observed roles agree with durable authorization; conflicting config or observations cannot silently change authority.

nodes.label: Generation checked journaled mutations
nodes.rationale: Mutations are journaled with caller, idempotency key and expected generation so conflicting requests against one generation yield at most one effect; failure to persist intent prevents the external action.

nodes.label: Durable intent before fencing and reconciliation of unknown outcomes
nodes.norm_label: durable intent before fencing and reconciliation of unknown outcomes
nodes.rationale: Lost responses can cause unsafe repeated operations; an inconclusive result keeps admission closed and prevents a second irreversible action.

nodes.label: RPO disclosure: known flush target or unknown loss window
nodes.norm_label: rpo disclosure: known flush target or unknown loss window
nodes.rationale: No implied zero data loss under asynchronous replication; switching to an unknown loss window requires a new plan and explicit approval.

nodes.label: Authenticated management transport (protected local or mTLS)
nodes.norm_label: authenticated management transport (protected local or mtls)
nodes.rationale: No unauthenticated loopback assumption: local port access is not identity; remote binding requires mTLS and explicit configuration.

nodes.label: Administration mutation retry contract
nodes.rationale: Retries resolve by actor, action and request ID; the same request returns the original operation ID even after lost response or restart, and reuse with a different target or payload conflicts, so one accepted request yields one logical operation.

nodes.label: Compare only equivalent pool modes at pinned releases
nodes.norm_label: compare only equivalent pool modes at pinned releases
nodes.rationale: A transaction pooling result cannot show a session pooler is slower when backend counts differ; feature lists and thread models are not proof, so each proposition is measured at a pinned release and configuration.

nodes.label: Competitor reference roles recommendation
nodes.rationale: Pgpool is the feature reference, PgBouncer the pooling efficiency reference, PgCat the Rust routing reference, Odyssey the concurrency and pool lifecycle reference, HAProxy only for endpoint availability. Reuse lessons and tests under license terms; do not transplant a whole implementation.

nodes.label: Equivalent profile benchmark method
nodes.rationale: POOL V1 is not a transaction pooler; reporting a transaction multiplexer's TPS beside a session pool with different backend occupancy is not an equivalent result, so experiments are separated and everything pinned.

nodes.label: Future multi proxy deployment
nodes.rationale: Losing controller authority must prevent mutations and must not cause every proxy to elect itself as PostgreSQL promoter.

nodes.label: Failure behavior (no transparent failover, no implicit replay)
nodes.norm_label: failure behavior (no transparent failover, no implicit replay)

nodes.label: Lease generation
nodes.rationale: A unique generation per lease keeps cancellation and delayed completions from affecting a reused backend.

nodes.label: Proposed public interfaces (FrameDecoder, SessionState, Lease, RouteDecision, ProbeObservation, OperationPlan)
nodes.norm_label: proposed public interfaces (framedecoder, sessionstate, lease, routedecision, probeobservation, operationplan)

nodes.label: External etcd for future coordination
nodes.rationale: Reuse established consensus; an embedded consensus library creates a larger storage and operations obligation.

nodes.label: Per lease virtual cancellation credentials
nodes.rationale: Real backend keys stay private and a backend is retired after any forwarded cancellation so uncertain delivery cannot reach a later lease; the promise is isolation across leases.

nodes.label: No automatic retry after dispatch
nodes.rationale: Once query bytes may have been sent the outcome is uncertain, so a backend failure surfaces as connection loss or the real server error; only initial acquisition before ReadyForQuery may pick another endpoint.

nodes.label: Drain, attach and quarantine operations
nodes.rationale: A successful probe cannot clear an operator's maintenance, detach or quarantine decision.

nodes.label: Local SQLite operation journal (single writer)
nodes.rationale: Persists approved writer, epoch, quarantine and operation intent; if durability is unavailable mutations fail closed. It does not establish distributed authority.

nodes.label: Operational ownership boundaries
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL owns WAL, durability and promotion primitives; operators own backups; systemd owns supervision; Proxmox owns VM lifecycle; external fencing excludes the old primary; POOL observes, controls admission and orchestrates authorized operations.

nodes.label: Bounded frame validation
nodes.rationale: Validate lengths, overflow, NUL boundaries, field counts and state legality before allocating; unsupported paths fail explicitly.

nodes.label: Authentication adapter (reviewed pgwire components)
nodes.rationale: POOL retains control of state, backend truth and advertised parameters rather than a server framework's canned values.

nodes.label: Data and protocol safety rules
nodes.rationale: Once bytes may have reached a backend the statement is never replayed, even if it appears idempotent; a lost COMMIT response is left for the application to reconcile.

nodes.label: Pgpool baseline modes and POOL dispositions
nodes.norm_label: pgpool baseline modes and pool dispositions

nodes.label: native_replication and snapshot_isolation modes (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Middleware replication introduces sequence, context value, large object and temporary table constraints, so it is a deferred feasibility decision.

nodes.label: Replication and routing option family (17 options)
nodes.norm_label: replication and routing option family (17 options)
nodes.rationale: Conservative policy equivalents; middleware replication controls deferred.

nodes.label: Independent review resolutions (seven approved fixes)
nodes.rationale: Another model critiqued the design; all seven recommended fixes were approved and applied. It is a design review, not a test, audit or certification.

nodes.label: pg_query parser with PostgreSQL 18 grammar
nodes.rationale: Native code is isolated and reviewed.

nodes.label: rustls and tokio-rustls with one crypto provider
nodes.norm_label: rustls and tokio-rustls with one crypto provider

nodes.label: Tokio runtime with bounded tasks and queues
nodes.norm_label: tokio runtime with bounded tasks and queues

nodes.label: CancellationEntry
nodes.rationale: Per lease opaque frontend token; real backend key data stays private and memory only.

nodes.label: PoolKey
nodes.rationale: Partition by full backend identity and configuration/credential generations so keys preserve actual database login identity.

nodes.label: Cancellation dispatch to the session-owning proxy
nodes.norm_label: cancellation dispatch to the session-owning proxy

nodes.label: Candidate CacheKey
nodes.rationale: Keys must include database, role, policy, session semantics and snapshot bounds so results never cross authorization boundaries.

nodes.label: Whole generation config validation and reload
nodes.norm_label: whole generation config validation and reload
nodes.rationale: An invalid reload retains the prior safe generation.

nodes.label: Retry only before initial lease and ReadyForQuery exposure
nodes.norm_label: retry only before initial lease and readyforquery exposure
nodes.rationale: Acquisition retry wording could imply session replacement; never retry after established session loss.

nodes.label: Authoritative barrier across every write path
nodes.norm_label: authoritative barrier across every write path
nodes.rationale: A POOL-only drain could imply a final WAL bound while direct writers remain; without the barrier the loss window is unknown.

nodes.label: Manual failover first; automatic failover and cache disabled
nodes.norm_label: manual failover first; automatic failover and cache disabled
nodes.rationale: Fixed safety boundary from the brief: manual failover first, automatic failover and caching stay disabled.

nodes.label: GA verification depth for data safety features
nodes.norm_label: ga verification depth for data safety features
nodes.rationale: Data safety features require verification, tests, independent review and documentation.

nodes.label: Operator map from verified principal and database to backend identity
nodes.norm_label: operator map from verified principal and database to backend identity
nodes.rationale: Credential selection authority was implicit; make it an explicit operator map with secret reference and generation.

nodes.label: Private backend keys and virtual frontend cancellation credentials
nodes.norm_label: private backend keys and virtual frontend cancellation credentials
nodes.rationale: Cancellation could arrive after lease reuse; serialize retirement and close the physical backend after forwarding.

nodes.label: Routing decision: primary default, explicit read only session profiles
nodes.norm_label: routing decision: primary default, explicit read only session profiles
nodes.rationale: Endpoint chosen at login, SQL admitted on pinned lease, lag screened at admission only, eventual reads, no primary fallback. Arbitrary sessions never move between servers; continuous staleness guarantees and transparent mixed-session routing are deferred.

nodes.label: Terminated SCRAM over TLS with optional mTLS and separate backend credentials
nodes.norm_label: terminated scram over tls with optional mtls and separate backend credentials
nodes.rationale: Frontend authentication is terminated at the proxy; backend credentials are separately provisioned. Implementation needs a feature spec.

nodes.label: Validation limits (no executable proxy exists)
nodes.rationale: Counts and link checks do not establish software correctness; no build, test, benchmark or drill has run.

nodes.label: Bounded admission, deadlines and graceful teardown
nodes.norm_label: bounded admission, deadlines and graceful teardown
nodes.rationale: Correctness and identity isolation precede throughput; all queues, buffers, tasks and external calls have explicit budgets.

nodes.label: Cancellation forwarded only through the live lease owner
nodes.norm_label: cancellation forwarded only through the live lease owner
nodes.rationale: Serialize cancellation with retirement and retire the physical backend after forwarding so later clients cannot be affected.

nodes.label: Reset and validate before reuse; close uncertain state
nodes.norm_label: reset and validate before reuse; close uncertain state
nodes.rationale: Unsafe reuse can leak identity or session state; reset uncertainty closes the socket instead of returning it idle.

nodes.label: Session pooling only (no transaction or statement multiplexing in V1)
nodes.norm_label: session pooling only (no transaction or statement multiplexing in v1)
nodes.rationale: Reuse clean backend sessions without changing the lifetime semantics of a connected frontend; one backend per connected frontend.

nodes.label: Caching disabled until a separate contract is approved and proven
nodes.norm_label: caching disabled until a separate contract is approved and proven
nodes.rationale: Incorrect keys or invalidation can expose or return invalid data; an attempt to enable caching is rejected under SEC-10.

nodes.label: Proposed protocol limits (64 KiB startup, 16 MiB message)
nodes.norm_label: proposed protocol limits (64 kib startup, 16 mib message)

nodes.label: SCRAM channel binding per terminated TLS channel
nodes.norm_label: scram channel binding per terminated tls channel

nodes.label: Variable length cancellation keys (protocol 3.2, up to 256 bytes)
nodes.norm_label: variable length cancellation keys (protocol 3.2, up to 256 bytes)
nodes.rationale: Hardcoding the historical four byte key is incorrect.

nodes.label: Rust tokio-postgres and postgres drivers (MVP gate)
nodes.norm_label: rust tokio-postgres and postgres drivers (mvp gate)

nodes.label: Features outside the initial support claim
nodes.norm_label: features outside the initial support claim
nodes.rationale: Protocol 2, legacy MD5, GSS, OAuth, logical replication clients and arbitrary extensions are excluded until qualified; a refused unsupported feature is different from silent corruption.

nodes.label: Proposed stopping rules
nodes.rationale: If parser coverage fails, route to primary or disable routing; if a session cannot be reset confidently, close the backend; if fencing cannot be verified, do not promote; fix measured bottlenecks before adding policies.

nodes.label: Close uncertain sessions cleanup policy
nodes.rationale: Unknown extension state may survive a nominal reset, so the default closes uncertain sessions with a positive allowlist for reusable profiles.

nodes.label: Independent backend credentials per mapped login identity
nodes.norm_label: independent backend credentials per mapped login identity
nodes.rationale: SCRAM verifier authentication on the frontend does not recover a reusable backend password; a global privileged role with SET ROLE is outside the initial contract.

nodes.label: Virtual per lease cancellation keys
nodes.rationale: Session manager owns virtual per lease frontend keys, keeps real backend keys private, serializes dispatch with retirement and closes the physical backend after a forwarded cancellation so there is no cross lease effect.

nodes.label: Endpoint failover via external load balancing or controlled VIP
nodes.norm_label: endpoint failover via external load balancing or controlled vip
nodes.rationale: Sockets do not migrate; document client reconnect behavior and never claim transaction migration.

nodes.label: Tracer Bullet build approach
nodes.rationale: Prove a real protocol path through the system before adding breadth.

nodes.label: Delivery slices
nodes.rationale: Start with one real client through the daemon to one primary, then thicken the same path; security, diagnostics and backpressure are built into each slice rather than deferred to Phase 4.

nodes.label: Estimation model (engineer weeks at 65 percent effective capacity)
nodes.norm_label: estimation model (engineer weeks at 65 percent effective capacity)
nodes.rationale: Order of magnitude ranges, no calendar dates; realistic elapsed = engineer_weeks / (2 * 0.65) as an allowance for review, coordination and discovery. Reestimate after the first two slices.

nodes.label: Established consensus for one operation authority
nodes.norm_label: established consensus for one operation authority
nodes.rationale: Independent controllers can create conflicting database operations; use established rather than custom consensus, and require fencing in addition because a controller lease is not a PostgreSQL fencing mechanism.

nodes.label: Query routing on local immutable snapshots
nodes.norm_label: query routing on local immutable snapshots
nodes.rationale: Queries must not perform a consensus round trip per request.

nodes.label: apps/pool daemon
nodes.rationale: The daemon maps control snapshots into the core route view, avoiding a hidden core to control dependency.

nodes.label: Documentation ownership
nodes.rationale: Each fact is updated in its owning file and linked from other views instead of maintaining contradictory copies.

nodes.label: Versioned local admin REST API (Axum)
nodes.rationale: Equivalent operator capabilities without copying PCP initially; remote administration needs mTLS and role authorization.

nodes.label: Tokio runtime with bounded tasks and channels
nodes.norm_label: tokio runtime with bounded tasks and channels
nodes.rationale: Fits long lived socket workloads; a thread per client is simpler but costly at high idle connection counts.

nodes.label: Hand written wire state machine on bytes and tokio::net
nodes.norm_label: hand written wire state machine on bytes and tokio::net
nodes.rationale: Keeps framing and state visible; a PostgreSQL client driver belongs in monitoring, not in the data path.

nodes.label: Data plane and control plane separation
nodes.norm_label: data plane and control plane separation
nodes.rationale: The data plane reads immutable topology snapshots and never does blocking journal work, infrastructure calls or consensus per query; control publishes snapshots only after validation.

nodes.label: admit_on_pinned_backend(frame, session_state, classification, policy)
nodes.rationale: Accepts or rejects without ever choosing a different backend; the session is not migrated.

nodes.label: Restricted read only replica profile
nodes.rationale: Naive read detection can send side effects to a replica or break session and read after write semantics, so replica selection happens only inside explicit read only profiles and unsafe or uncertain operations are rejected.

nodes.label: Replica eligibility filter (role, identity, freshness, maintenance, lag)
nodes.norm_label: replica eligibility filter (role, identity, freshness, maintenance, lag)
nodes.rationale: Read capacity is useful only when selection excludes stale, draining or incorrectly identified nodes; eligibility is rechecked before acquisition completes.

nodes.label: Primary fallback disabled in V1
nodes.rationale: Enabling primary fallback requires a new decision and independently enforced read restrictions that survive promotion; no case silently selects a writable primary for a replica profile.

nodes.label: Backend cleanup and reset (rollback, DISCARD ALL, idle ReadyForQuery)
nodes.norm_label: backend cleanup and reset (rollback, discard all, idle readyforquery)
nodes.rationale: DISCARD ALL is not a universal guarantee for extension state, so sessions with unknown state, active COPY or failed cleanup are closed.

nodes.label: Backend connection lifecycle state machine (Connecting, Idle, Leased, Cleaning, Draining, Closed)
nodes.norm_label: backend connection lifecycle state machine (connecting, idle, leased, cleaning, draining, closed)

nodes.label: Transaction pooling (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Needs a feature compatibility contract for GUCs, prepared statements, portals, temp objects, LISTEN, locks, cursors, sequences and extension state.

nodes.label: Deferred features (cache, automatic failover, native replication, multiplexing)
nodes.norm_label: deferred features (cache, automatic failover, native replication, multiplexing)

nodes.label: POOL (PostgreSQL 18 proxy, session pooler and cluster manager in Rust)
nodes.norm_label: pool (postgresql 18 proxy, session pooler and cluster manager in rust)

nodes.label: Durable approved writer authority
nodes.rationale: Observed PostgreSQL role is always a fresh observation while approved writer identity is a durable authorization decision; neither substitutes for the other and admission requires both to agree. The writer is never inferred solely from pg_is_in_recovery() = false.

nodes.label: Login time backend selection on pinned lease
nodes.norm_label: login time backend selection on pinned lease
nodes.rationale: The backend is chosen from profile and fresh topology before SQL is available; the parser is not an input to initial selection and later operations are admitted or rejected without changing endpoint.

nodes.label: Cluster features F-061 to F-066 (registry, topology)
nodes.norm_label: cluster features f-061 to f-066 (registry, topology)

nodes.label: Coverage limits of the feature inventory
nodes.norm_label: coverage limits of the feature inventory
nodes.rationale: No audit of every C path, undocumented alias or build flag is claimed. A full parity claim requires pinned source and binary hashes, reconciled manual entries, differential tests and rows marked Tested with evidence. Excluded features stay in the denominator.

nodes.label: F-024 Transaction mode pooling (refused; session pooling only)
nodes.norm_label: f-024 transaction mode pooling (refused; session pooling only)
nodes.rationale: Future multiplexing needs a separate contract.

nodes.label: F-053 Lag filtering and primary fallback (fallback disabled in V1)
nodes.norm_label: f-053 lag filtering and primary fallback (fallback disabled in v1)

nodes.label: F-056 Primary standby role observation
nodes.rationale: Observe role independently of reachability; reachable wrong-role node excluded.

nodes.label: F-060 Network partitions (health changes eligibility only)
nodes.norm_label: f-060 network partitions (health changes eligibility only)

nodes.label: F-065 Primary identification (durably approved writer with fresh evidence)
nodes.norm_label: f-065 primary identification (durably approved writer with fresh evidence)
nodes.rationale: Only the durably approved writer with fresh matching role and cluster evidence can accept writes; two observed primaries close affected admission.

nodes.label: F-075 Automatic failover (disabled in V1)
nodes.rationale: Disabled initially; a future independent safety case is required. Health failure cannot trigger promotion and explicit attempts to enable it fail.

nodes.label: F-088 Optional memory cache (result caching disabled in V1)
nodes.norm_label: f-088 optional memory cache (result caching disabled in v1)
nodes.rationale: Any future cache needs a separate decision; requests to enable the unsupported feature fail.

nodes.label: HA features F-081 to F-087 (multiple proxies, quorum, watchdog equivalent)
nodes.norm_label: ha features f-081 to f-087 (multiple proxies, quorum, watchdog equivalent)
nodes.rationale: Established external consensus, no custom algorithm; failure evidence is distinct from authority.

nodes.label: Initial V1 exclusions
nodes.rationale: Transaction/statement multiplexing, session migration, automatic promotion, native and snapshot replication, logical replication routing, result caching, PCP wire compatibility, pgpool_adm compatibility and a dashboard are excluded; rows preserve the future decision rather than claiming implementation.

nodes.label: Clustering mode features F-094 to F-099
nodes.norm_label: clustering mode features f-094 to f-099

nodes.label: PCP operation equivalents F-120 to F-134
nodes.norm_label: pcp operation equivalents f-120 to f-134

nodes.label: Pgpool-II 4.7.3 baseline

nodes.label: Pooling features F-023 to F-032 (session pooling)
nodes.norm_label: pooling features f-023 to f-032 (session pooling)

nodes.norm_label: f-067 manual plan and promotion (operator plan plus verified fence)
